title: Academic Coordinator for the EUROfusion Project
description:
SDU Center for Large Structure Production (LSP), part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI) at University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one funded Academic Staff position, to be project administrator for the EUROfusion project. The temporary position will be vacant from 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, until 31 December 2027. Main work location is Odense/Denmark at SDU and Odense Havn (Odense Port).

Work environment

The candidate will be part of SDU Center for Large Structure Production (LSP). LSP’s central ambition is to provide a physical “go-to” lab for companies in the sectors maritime, construction and energy to carry out research, development, and testing of novel solutions in the production of large structures, such as buildings, ships and offshore platforms. In this context, the candidate is expected to work closely with our industrial partners on application-oriented use cases, while helping to commission and operate the unique set of equipment of the center. 

LSP is closely working together the companies at Odense Havn and similar partners making large structures across Denmark and Europe. LSP is integrated with the Odense Robotics Cluster involving startups and established companies in robotics. We are a team of currently about 24 researchers, engineers and PhD students, specialized in robot solutions involving modelling, simulation, and control of advanced robot technologies (systems and services) for application-oriented industrial applications. 

Our group is involved in a variety of national and European projects and features a strong network of academic and industrial partners. We solve challenging research problems derived from real-life challenges by implementing novel robot solutions. We value teamwork, professional diligence, enthusiasm for robotics and the drive to adopt new skills and extended responsibilities. We offer an open, international team, with flexible work organization and support for individual development.

Job description

The candidate will be project administrator for the EUROfusion project. Jointly, and together with the rest of the team around this project, this goes for other institutes and departments of SDU TEK together with partners from ITER and EUROfusion. 

Profile and requirements

The candidate is expected to have the following qualifications:

  • Good communication and collaborative skills

  • Good English and Danish skills, both written and spoken

  • Can work independently and have a good overview

  • IT skills and being good at developing and maintaining procedures

  • Background in engineering will be useful, e.g. involving handling of 3D models

Contact information

For further information, please contact Professor Christian Schlette via email (chsch@mmmi.sdu.dk) or on LinkedIn (www.linkedin.com/in/christian-schlette/).

Application deadline: November 30, 2026 at 23:59 o'clock. 

Employment shall take place in accordance with the framework agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

"Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.”

Application must include cover letter, CV and certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out. 

You can only apply for the position at – https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/job-sdu. 

All attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. Cover letter and CV can contain max. 5 Mb.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.

title: Associate Professors in AI Engineering
description:
SDU Centre for Industrial Software in Sønderborg, part of the Software Engineering units at SDU situated at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one or more positions within AI Engineering. The positions are open from beginning of 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates. 

The application deadline is December 7, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET).

 

What we offer

With a position at SDU, you will:

  • be part of one of our dynamic research centres with both a national and international profile, while working in areas of tremendous potential and societal relevance;

  • join collaborations across the university, as well as with national, international, and industrial research partners;

  • help establish joint innovation projects in close collaboration with industry and the local society;

  • help build up the research and educational environment;

  • contribute to the teaching programmes in Software Engineering at the highest level for undergraduate and graduate students at SDU;

  • join a harmonious workplace environment that is conducive to productivity, promotes creativity, and rewards and recognizes individuals and group achievement;

  • have the opportunity to live and work in one of the happiest countries in the world that also offers excellent and free health and education systems.

 

What we expect

The focus of the SDU Centre for Industrial Software is research and education in software engineering, embedded systems, cyber-security and AI engineering. We see these areas complementing each other to make way for the engineering of the next generation of reliable, intelligent and embedded software solutions. We are particularly interested in software operated in real life, systems that adapt at runtime, span embedded devices, edge infrastructure and the cloud, that people work with and trust, and that increasingly answer to regulation. This includes understanding how new technologies change the engineering of products and software infrastructures.

The positions are open in any of the AI engineering research areas of interest to the centres, which include:

  • AI Engineering (e.g. multi-modal machine learning)

  • AI integration in mobile, wearable and embedded platforms

  • Human-AI collaboration in the context of mobile, wearable and embedded platforms

  • Domain-oriented AI Engineering (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing).

 

Who we are looking for

We expect applicants to hold a PhD in artificial intelligence, software engineering, computer science or a closely related discipline. For associate professors we expect a research and teaching record corresponding to several years of independent work after the PhD, including documented teaching and supervision experience.

We are looking for candidates who have demonstrated research excellence appropriate to their career stage, who show a clear path towards an independent and internationally recognised research programme, and who are able and willing to contribute to competitive national and international funding applications. We also expect an interest in working across disciplines, in supervising students and junior researchers, and in teaching and advising in software engineering at all levels.

We particularly welcome applications from candidates who publish in leading venues in the field. If your work is more domain oriented and you therefore publish in leading venues within a specific domain, you are also very welcome to apply.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a requirement, and successful applicants will be offered Danish language courses.

 

Workplace description

The University of Southern Denmark

The University of Southern Denmark is one of the youngest universities in Denmark, founded in 1966. The university is founded around the goal of providing the right knowledge at the right time to support society. The university targets major, complex societal problems of a cross-disciplinary nature such as climate, welfare, health and technology, tackling these in collaboration across faculties.

The Faculty of Engineering

The Faculty of Engineering is driven by the urge to create value for and with society, by curiosity and by the will to create that which only a few could imagine would be possible. Through research, education and collaboration, it is the ambition of the faculty to nurture talent, address challenges, create possibilities, and promote sustainable development. The faculty is strongly engaged with national and international industries and organizations over a broad range of technical domains.

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The department is the 2nd largest department at SDU, with more than 230 staff members and 1500 students. The institute has over the last decades expanded its activities in interactive technologies, artificial intelligence, and software engineering including building several strong research centres at the SDU campuses in Odense, Sønderborg and Vejle. Thereby, the institute today covers a wide range of areas in robotics, software, AI, and applied informatics.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Sønderborg.

 

Curious?

If you are interested in learning more about the positions, please contact:

  • Torben Worm (Head of Centres): tow@mmmi.sdu.dk

  • Mikkel Baun Kjærgaard (Vice-Head of Centres): mbkj@mmmi.sdu.dk

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

 

Application procedure

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

  • Cover letter.

  • Curriculum Vitae.

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (copy of original and official English translation).

  • Complete list of publications.

  • Up to five most relevant publications to the position.

  • A research statement.

  • Teaching Portfolio documenting teaching, learning, and supervision qualifications and approach. Any format is acceptable; see the Faculty's teaching portfolio page for inspiration.

  • Up to three reference letters may be included (optional).

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included (optional).

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration no.) must be crossed out. All PDF files must be unlocked and allow binding and may not be password protected.

UPLOAD GUIDE: Cover letter shall be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae shall be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max. 5 MB). All other documents shall be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max. 10 files of max. 50 MB per file).

 

The application deadline is December 7, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET).

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.

 

Employment terms

Appointment as an associate professor is permanent.

Employment as an associate professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level as well as scientific and teaching qualifications commensurate with the position as an associate professor. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for associate professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

title: Postdoc in Mechatronic Design for Remotely Operated Vehicles
description:
Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites application for an 18-month postdoc position within Mechatronic Design for Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs). The position is available from March 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed upon with the successful candidates.

 

What we offer 

Successful candidates will join an interdisciplinary engineering research environment at SDU Sønderborg and contribute to the development of ROVs and associated subsea mechatronics. The work combines engineering design, numerical modelling, prototyping, fabrication, integration, and experimental validation in laboratory and marine environments.

The positions offer opportunities to:

  • Develop and evaluate mechatronic components, subsystems, and integrated ROV platforms.

  • Design underwater actuation mechanisms, transmissions, structural components, and pressure-resistant enclosures, including sealing and mechanical interfaces.

  • Integrate underwater sensors, actuators, embedded electronics, and control hardware.

  • Perform CAD modelling, engineering analysis, simulations, design optimisation, and prototype fabrication.

  • Conduct laboratory and field testing to improve the performance, reliability, and robustness of subsea mechatronic technologies.

  • Publish research in international scientific journals and conferences, collaborate with research partners, and contribute to student supervision where relevant.

 

What we expect 

Applicants must hold a PhD degree in mechatronics, mechanical engineering, robotics, marine engineering, or a closely related discipline at the time of employment. We seek motivated researchers with strong mechatronic design skills and hands-on experience in developing, integrating, and testing electromechanical systems.

Applicants should have demonstrated expertise in mechatronic design and practical experience in several of the following areas:

  • Mechanical and mechatronic design, including actuation, transmissions, structural design, and electromechanical integration.

  • CAD and engineering modelling or analysis, such as finite element analysis, multibody dynamics, or related methods.

  • Integration of sensors, actuators, embedded electronics, and control hardware.

  • Rapid prototyping, additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and experimental development.

  • Experimental testing, instrumentation, data acquisition, system characterisation, and troubleshooting.

  • Basic programming and control using tools such as Python, C/C++, MATLAB/Simulink, or ROS/ROS 2.

Experience in subsea engineering, ROV development, underwater actuation, pressure-resistant enclosures, waterproofing, sealing, or marine instrumentation is an advantage but not a requirement. Applicants should have a publication record appropriate to their career stage, sound scientific judgement, good written and spoken English, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

 

Workplace description 

The positions will be based at the Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM), Department of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, University of Southern Denmark, in Sønderborg. The research environment brings together expertise in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, modelling, control, and experimental engineering.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Sønderborg. 

 

Further information 

For further information about the position, please contact:

  • Lars Duggen, Head of Unit, SDU Mechatronics (CIM), at duggen@sdu.dk

  • Mrudul Chellapurath, Assistant Professor, at mrch@sdu.dk

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

  • Motivated application.

  • Curriculum Vitae. 

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

  • Complete list of publications highlighting the publications most relevant to the position.

  • A research statement.

  • References/reference letters may also be included.

  • Documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is December 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 18-month period, and the preferred start date is from March 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding. 

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time of registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

title: Library and Digital Media Officer
description:
Job Title: Library and Digital Media Officer

Job Type: Part-time (with possibility of full-time conversion) | Workplace: Copenhagen, Denmark | Employer: China Cultural Center in Copenhagen

 

About the Organization

The China Cultural Center in Copenhagen is an official institution dedicated to promoting cultural and tourism exchanges between China and Denmark at both governmental and grassroots levels. We organize cultural events, facilitate people-to-people exchanges, and collaborate with Danish institutions and travel trade partners to enhance mutual understanding and cooperation.

We are currently seeking a motivated and experienced professional to join our team and to serve as an important communication window for promoting Chinese culture to Danish and international audiences.

 

Job Description

The Library and Digital Media Officer is responsible for the management and operation of the China Cultural Center's digital media platforms and library, as well as the promotion of the Center's cultural activities and public services.

 

Key Responsibilities

 ⑴ Social Media Management and Digital Communications

Manage and maintain the Center's social media accounts and digital platforms, including WeChat Official Account, Facebook, Instagram and the Center's official website. 

Plan, create, edit and publish communication materials, including news articles, event announcements, promotional posts, photographs, videos and other digital content.

Develop and implement social media content plans in accordance with the Center's events and communication objectives.

Monitor platform performance, analyse engagement and audience data, and continuously improve content quality and online visibility.

Coordinate photography, video recording, editing and the archiving of promotional materials for the Center's activities.

 ⑵ Library Management and Public Services

Oversee the daily operations of the Center's library, including book classification, cataloguing, registration, lending, returns and collection management.

Establish and maintain library management procedures and reader services, including opening arrangements, reservations and visitor reception.

Actively promote the opening of the library to the general public and expand its readership among local residents and communities.

Plan and organise reading promotion activities, book-sharing sessions, cultural talks and other public cultural activities.

Promote the library's resources and services to increase its visibility and accessibility within the local community.

⑶ Cultural Communications and General Support

Support the promotion and publicity of the Center's cultural events, exhibitions, performances, lectures and cultural exchange activities.

Photograph cultural events and create visual content for the Center's promotional and communication purposes.

Participate in developing communication strategies, preparing promotional materials, writing copy and producing multimedia content.

Assist in establishing and maintaining relationships with local communities, schools, cultural institutions and other relevant organisations to expand partnerships and promote public cultural services.

Undertake other related duties as assigned by the Center.

 

Essential:

1. Language: Fluent proficiency in both Chinese and English (written and spoken).

2. Industry Knowledge: Professional knowledge of social media management and digital platform operations. Proficiency in using standard office software and applications.

3. Paper Work Ability: written communication and analytical reporting skills.

4. Education: Bachelor's degree or above.

5. Background Check: An acceptable criminal record check is required and Applicants must have the legal right to work in Denmark.

6. Health: Ability to provide a health certificate as required by the employer.

 

Preferred:

1. Proficiency in Danish is a strong advantage.

 

Work Authorization

During the interview stage, candidates will be asked to confirm their current residence status in Denmark. For positions involving international travel, verification of legal work authorization may be required prior to final offer.

 

Selection Process & Interview

To apply for this position, please submit the following to our email:

① Your CV/resume;

② A written proposal outlining how you would develop and manage the media and digital communication platforms of the China Cultural Center in Copenhagen.

 (format: Word or PDF)

 

Selection Timeline:

1. Applications will be screened on a rolling basis, and shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

2. If you have not received an email response by 31 December, 2026, please assume that your application has not been shortlisted for an interview.

 

Special Terms of Employment

This position starts on a part-time basis. The Center may offer a one-year full-time contract, based on work performance and business needs. The final interpretation of these employment terms shall reside with the Center.

 

Contact for Applications

China Cultural Center in Copenhagen

Email:[info@ccccph.org]

Subject line for applications: "Library and Digital Media Officer – [Your Name]"

We look forward to receiving your application!

title: Erfaren kok søges til China Palace i Aarhus N
description:

  • Kan kommunikere på mindst ét af følgende sprog: dansk, engelsk eller kinesisk

  • Et godt arbejdsmiljø med fokus på samarbejde og gensidig respekt

  • En varieret arbejdsdag i en restaurant med mange forskellige asiatiske retter

  • Løn efter kvalifikationer og erfaring

China Palace i Aarhus N tilbyder en stor asiatisk buffet med et udvalg af varme asiatiske retter, sushi og Mongolian BBQ. Derudover serverer vi à la carte og tilbyder takeaway.

Vi lægger vægt på god madkvalitet, effektiv drift og et godt samarbejde mellem medarbejderne.

Vi afholder samtaler løbende og afslutter rekrutteringen, når den rette kandidat er fundet.

Ansøgning

Send din ansøgning og dit CV til:

pinglin68@live.dk

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig!

ENGELSIH BELOW!

Experienced Chef Wanted – China Palace, Aarhus N

China Palace is looking for a skilled and motivated chef with experience in Asian cuisine. We are seeking a responsible and dedicated employee who can contribute to the daily kitchen operations and help provide our guests with a great dining experience.

You will be an important part of our kitchen team and work closely with our head chef.

Your responsibilities

  • Assist with the daily management and coordination of kitchen operations together with the head chef

  • Prepare and cook Asian dishes for our buffet, à la carte menu and takeaway orders

  • Prepare ingredients and organize daily food production

  • Distribute tasks and coordinate kitchen staff when needed

  • Maintain consistent food quality, taste and presentation

  • Ensure that kitchen hygiene and food safety standards are followed

We expect you to

  • Have good cooking skills and solid experience in Asian cuisine

  • Be familiar with Asian ingredients and different cooking techniques

  • Have experience working in a busy kitchen and be able to handle pressure

  • Work independently, stay organized and take responsibility

  • Be reliable, flexible and committed to your work

  • Have good teamwork skills and contribute to a positive working environment

  • Be able to communicate in at least one of the following languages: Danish, English or Chinese

We offer

  • A permanent full-time position of 37 hours per week

  • Freedom with responsibility and the opportunity to participate in daily kitchen planning

  • A good working environment based on teamwork and mutual respect

  • Varied daily work in a restaurant serving a wide selection of Asian dishes

  • Salary based on qualifications and experience

  • Start as soon as possible

About China Palace

title: Postdoc in Whole-Ship Energy Modelling and Maritime Decarbonization
description:
SDU Mechanical Engineering (SDU ME), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for an 18-month postdoctoral position in thermodynamics-based whole-ship energy modelling. The position is expected to start in March 2027, with the specific start date to be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

 

What we offer

You will join a research project titled Thermodynamics-Based Whole-Ship Energy Mapping for Retrofit-Oriented Maritime Decarbonization (STERN) funded by Den Danske Maritime Fond. STERN addresses a practical maritime engineering challenge: improvements to individual components do not necessarily result in optimal energy performance for the vessel as a whole. The project will develop physically consistent steady-state and dynamic energy models to quantify interactions among propulsion, auxiliary equipment, cooling and heating systems, waste heat and energy storage under representative operating conditions.

The postdoc will work within an interdisciplinary SDU team led by Assistant Professor Baris Burak Kanbur, together with Professor Marie Lützen and Associate Professor Paride Gullo, and collaborate with maritime partners including the shipping company Hafnia, DESMI and Fredericia Maskinmesterskole (FMS). ShippingLab will support maritime knowledge exchange and outreach. The position offers opportunities for independent scientific development, high-quality publications and close interaction with industry.

 

Main research activities

  • Develop modular steady-state thermodynamic and energy-balance models for whole-ship energy mapping, covering fuel input, propulsion, auxiliary power, thermal loads, heat rejection and recoverable energy streams.

  • Extend these models to dynamic energy simulations representing time-varying engine loads, operational profiles, mode transitions and relevant subsystem interactions.

  • Model and analyze selected marine subsystems and energy-integration pathways, including propulsion-related energy demand, waste heat recovery, HVAC, cooling/heating optimization, thermal storage and battery storage.

  • Use representative vessel and component data, engineering correlations and partner feedback to check model assumptions, quantify uncertainty and compare baseline and retrofit-oriented scenarios in terms of energy use and emissions.

  • Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, project meetings, reporting and dissemination of non-confidential results.

 

Required qualifications

  • A PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Thermal Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline (completed by the date of employment).

  • A strong foundation in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics (thermo-fluids) and energy-system analysis.

  • Demonstrated experience in numerical thermodynamic or energy-system modelling, including steady-state analysis and time-dependent/dynamic simulation.

  • Programming or modelling skills in MATLAB, Python or comparable scientific computing environments, with the ability to develop and document reproducible models.

  • Knowledge of waste heat recovery, refrigeration/HVAC, cooling and heating networks, energy storage or component performance maps.

  • Ability to conduct independent research, work with an interdisciplinary team and communicate research results effectively in English.

 

Qualifications considered an advantage

  • Experience with marine engines, propulsion systems, ship energy systems or vessel operating profiles.

  • Experience with dynamic simulation and control environment like MATLAB Simulink, Modelica/Dymola or equivalent modelling frameworks can also be considered.

  • Knowledge of advanced control engineering, optimization or model-based control approaches, and experience collaborating with industrial partners.

 

Workplace description 

The position is full-time at SDU ME and located at the SDU main campus in Odense. SDU Odense is the university’s largest campus and provides a strong framework for interdisciplinary research, teaching, and innovation. You will be part of a modern workplace with high professionalism, strong academic communities, and a commitment to diversity and equal opportunities. SDU also offers dedicated support for International Staff. Learn more about careers and work life at SDU here: Careers at SDU.

SDU ME is part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME) at the Faculty of Engineering. The research activities at SDU ME span widely from fluid mechanics, multi-physics simulation and optimization to condition monitoring and structural dynamics, composite materials, mechanical design, and naval architecture and marine engineering. 

The research environment combines thermo-fluid science, energy engineering and computational modelling, with collaboration across SDU and external maritime partners. The successful candidate will contribute to an industry-informed research project while working closely with academic colleagues and maritime experts. The research group is also part of the broader maritime research community at SDU, providing opportunities for transdisciplinary collaboration across faculties through the SDU Maritime Centre.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Odense. 

 

Further information 

For academic enquiries about the position and the STERN project, please contact Assistant Professor Baris Burak Kanbur (babk@sdu.dk ) SDU Mechanical Engineering.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

  • One page motivation letter.

  • Curriculum Vitae. 

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

  • Complete list of publications.

  • Three publications most relevant to the position.

  • Name of three references.

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is January 1, 2027, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 18-month period. The preferred start date is in early 2027 (exact date to be confirmed). Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. title: Assistant, Tenure-track Assistant, and Associate Professorships in Interactive Technology and AI Engineering
description:
SDU Centre for Software Technology in Vejle, part of the Software Engineering units at SDU situated at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one or more positions within interaction technology and AI engineering. The positions are open from beginning of 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates.

What we offer

With a position at SDU, you will:

  • be part of one of our dynamic research centres with both a national and international profile, while working in areas of tremendous potential and societal relevance;

  • join collaborations across the university, as well as with national, international, and industrial research partners;

  • help establish joint innovation projects in close collaboration with industry and the local society;

  • help build up the research and educational environment;

  • contribute to the teaching programmes in Interactive Technology and Software Engineering at the highest level for undergraduate and graduate students at SDU;

  • join a harmonious workplace environment that is conducive to productivity, promotes creativity, and rewards and recognizes individuals and group achievement;

  • have the opportunity to live and work in one of the happiest countries in the world that also offers excellent and free health and education systems.

What we expect

The focus of the SDU Centre for Software Technology is research and education in software engineering, interactive technology and artificial intelligence. We see these areas complementing each other to make way for the engineering of the next generation of reliable, intelligent and interactive software solutions. We are particularly interested in software operated in real life, systems that adapt at runtime, span embedded devices, edge infrastructure and the cloud, that people work with and trust, and that increasingly answer to regulation. This includes understanding how AI technologies and data-informed software development with a human-centred perspective can change the engineering of products and software infrastructures.

The positions are open in any of the interaction technology and AI engineering research areas of interest to the centres, which include:

  • Human-Computer Interaction and Design

  • Interactive Systems Engineering

  • AI-based User Interface Technology (e.g. generative user interfaces)

  • Human-AI collaboration (e.g. robotics)

  • Human-Centred Technology Ethics and Human-Centred AI Ethics

  • Human-Centred and Socio-Technical Software Engineering

  • Domain-oriented Interaction Technology (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing)

  • User Interaction Technologies (e.g., augmented reality and wearable technology)

  • AI Engineering (e.g. multi-modal machine learning)

  • Domain-oriented AI Engineering (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing).

Who we are looking for

We are looking for candidates who have demonstrated research excellence appropriate to their career stage, who show a clear path towards an independent and internationally recognised research programme, and who are able and willing to contribute to competitive national and international funding applications. We also expect an interest in working across disciplines, in supervising students and junior researchers, and in teaching and advising in software engineering at all levels.

We particularly welcome applications from candidates who publish in leading venues in the field, such as CHI (Human Factors in Computing Systems), DIS (Designing Interactive Systems), CSCW (Computer-Supported Cooperative Work), NordiCHI, UIST (User Interface Software & Technology), IUI, HRI (Human-Robot Interaction), TEI (Tangible Embedded Embodied Interaction), IDC (Interaction Design & Children), UbiComp (Ubiquitous Computing), PerCom, EICS, AAAI, WWW, ACM CIKM; and in journals such as IMWUT and IEEE TASE. If your work is more domain oriented and you therefore publish in leading venues within a specific domain, you are also very welcome to apply.

We expect applicants to hold a PhD in human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence, software engineering, computer science or a closely related discipline, completed before the application deadline. 

For the tenure-track assistant professor positions we expect at least one year of research experience beyond the PhD, gained in academia, at a research institute or in industry. Applicants must demonstrate a higher level of achievement in research and related professional activities than generally expected of assistant professor applicants, as well as the potential to attain international research excellence within their field and meet the criteria for employment as an associate professor during the tenure track assistant professorship.

For the associate professor positions we expect a research and teaching record corresponding to several years of independent work after the PhD, including documented teaching and supervision experience.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a requirement, and successful applicants will be offered Danish language courses.

Workplace description

The University of Southern Denmark

The University of Southern Denmark is one of the youngest universities in Denmark, founded in 1966. The university is founded around the goal of providing the right knowledge at the right time to support society. The university targets major, complex societal problems of a cross-disciplinary nature such as climate, welfare, health and technology, tackling these in collaboration across faculties.

The Faculty of Engineering

The Faculty of Engineering is driven by the urge to create value for and with society, by curiosity and by the will to create that which only a few could imagine would be possible. Through research, education and collaboration, it is the ambition of the faculty to nurture talent, address challenges, create possibilities, and promote sustainable development. The faculty is strongly engaged with national and international industries and organizations over a broad range of technical domains.

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The department is the 2nd largest department at SDU, with more than 230 staff members and 1500 students. The institute has over the last decades expanded its activities in interactive technologies, artificial intelligence, and software engineering including building several strong research centres at the SDU campuses in Odense and Sønderborg and with the new centre also in Vejle. Thereby, the institute today covers a wide range of areas in robotics, software, AI, and applied informatics.

Hear about the vision behind SDU Vejle - and why you as a researcher should consider joining the journey.

Curious?

If you are interested in learning more about the position, please contact:

  • Torben Worm (Head of Centres): tow@mmmi.sdu.dk

  • Mikkel Baun Kjærgaard (Vice-Head of Centres): mbkj@mmmi.sdu.dk

  • Noura Lena Howell: nouh@mmmi.sdu.dk

  • Aparna Varde: apva@mmmi.sdu.dk

Application procedure

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

  • Cover letter.

  • Curriculum Vitae.

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (copy of original and official English translation).

  • Complete list of publications.

  • Up to five most relevant publications to the position.

  • A research statement.

  • For assistant professor applicants: Summary and documentation of experience in teaching

  • For associate professor applicants: Teaching Portfolio documenting teaching, learning, and supervision qualifications and approach. Any format is acceptable; see the Faculty's teaching portfolio page for inspiration.

  • Up to three reference letters may be included (optional).

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included (optional).

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration no.) must be crossed out. All PDF files must be unlocked and allow binding and may not be password protected.

The application deadline is December 15, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET).

 

Tenure Track at the Faculty of Engineering, SDUThe Faculty of Engineering at SDU offers an attractive tenure track programme aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area.

Candidates enter at the assistant professor level and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position as associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee.  

This evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential. Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. The evaluation may also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities.

As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution.

The programme includes annual performance reviews, a midterm evaluation by an expert panel, and a final academic assessment. If the final assessment is positive, the candidate will progress to a permanent position as associate professor. If the final evaluation is negative, the assistant professor may request one additional assessment within the last six months of employment. The tenure track period may be extended in connection with maternity, paternity, or adoption leave.

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period. 

Appointment as a tenure track assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 4-year period, with guaranteed assessment for a permanent position as associate professor during the final year of employment.

Appointment as an associate professor is permanent.

Employment requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment, as well as scientific and teaching qualifications commensurate with the position level. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state included the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor, tenure track assistant professor, or associate professor as described therein. 

During employment at assistant professor level (incl. tenure track), the candidate will complete the Lecturer Training Programme.

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

title: Associate professor in Artificial Intelligence for Medical Applications at SDU Robotics
description:
To support our advancements in deep learning and AI methods for medical image and clinical data analysis SDU Robotics invites applications for one or more associate professor position(s). The starting date is in March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter and will be agreed with the successful candidates. The workplace is at SDU's main campus in Odense, Denmark, and the work is expected to be primarily onsite.

 

What we offer

  • An exciting opportunity to work at the cutting edge of robotics for real-world applications.

  • A collaborative and supportive work environment that encourages innovation and creativity.

  • Opportunities for professional growth and leadership.

  • Access to state-of-the-art technology and resources.

 

Job descriptionThe successful candidates will contribute to the unit’s current and future research projects and teaching activities. Key responsibilities include, for example to:

  • Be able to collaborate with our experts and colleagues from SDU Robotics in the further development of our core technologies. 

  • Be deeply involved in our regular coordination and joint evolvement of research and project activities. 

  • Raise funding and manage research projects. 

  • Design and conduct lab experiments. 

  • Participate in the practicalities of actual industrial applications. 

  • Organize, plan and conduct excellent teaching for undergraduate and graduate courses. 

  • Independently supervise project courses, and BSc, MSc and PhD thesis projects. 

The position as an associate professor involves primary responsibilities related to research (including the obligation to publish and disseminate scientific knowledge) and research-based teaching (including examination duties) – research and teaching obligations equally. Additionally, the role may encompass knowledge exchange with society, including participation in public debates. Furthermore, it may entail responsibilities such as research management, curriculum development, guidance, supervision, and scholarly assessment. The university determines the specific allocation of tasks, and the emphasis on these tasks may vary over time.

 

Profile and requirementsThe candidates will participate in SDU Robotics' comprehensive research, and the position requires research experience within artificial intelligence and deep learning for medical applications. This includes documented knowledge within some of the following technologies/areas:

  • Deep learning-based classification, segmentation and detection in 2D and 3D medical images.

  • Machine learning methods for analysis of clinical data.

  • Explainable and interpretable AI methods for medical decision support.

The candidates must have a relevant PhD degree (e.g. in computer science, engineering or a related field) and are expected to have most of the following qualifications:

  • Research demonstrated by publications in relevant scientific journals and conferences.

  • Experience in acquiring and coordinating publicly and/or privately funded projects.

  • Strong track record of directly engaging with clinical or industrial partners in application-oriented projects and/or a relevant international network for research and collaboration activities.

  • Experience with teaching and independently supervising project courses, and BSc and MSc thesis projects.

  • Experience in teaching AI courses for medical image analysis.

Preferably, the candidates have experience with:

  • Medical image analysis

  • Analysis of clinical and healthcare data

  • Explainable AI

  • Experimental design and validation of AI-based systems

Furthermore, the successful candidate is expected to:

  • Be able to work well and communicate expert knowledge in an interdisciplinary team. 

  • Have the ability of working independently.

  • Have high self-motivation to learn. 

  • Have a strong sense of responsibility.

  • Have excellent communication skills in English speaking and writing. 

In the assessment of candidates, consideration will be given to: 

  • Research demonstrated by publications in relevant scientific journals and conferences.

  • Experience in interdisciplinary research collaboration.

  • Teaching experience.

  • A relevant international network for research and collaboration activities, research experience abroad.

  • Experience in attracting funding for research projects and demonstrated experience in research leadership.

 

Research environment The candidate will be integrated into the unit SDU Robotics, which is involved in a variety of national and European projects and features a strong network of academic and industrial partners. We are a team of currently appr. 60 researchers and engineers specialized in research and development of robot solutions and advanced robot systems within the medical, welfare and industrial domain. 

We value teamwork, professional diligence, enthusiasm for robotics and the drive to adopt new skills and extended responsibilities. We offer an open, international team with flexible work organization and support for individual development.

SDU Robotics is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), and located at the main Campus in Odense, at the core of the Odense Robotics Cluster involving 120+ startups and established companies in robotics. 

The aim of the group is to solve challenging research problems derived from real-life challenges by implementing novel robot solutions. We participate in implementing the results achieved in real solutions with end users like national hospitals, LEGO, Novo Nordisk and Universal Robots.

We look forward to receiving your application and to supporting your growth as a researcher in SDU Robotics.

description: Every day, we get opportunities to make a positive impact - on our colleagues, partners, customers, and society. Together, we're pioneering the solutions of the future and unlocking the full potential of precious resources. Trusted to act on initiative, we challenge conventional thinking to develop world-leading technologies that inspire progress in vital areas, including energy, food, water, and shipping.  As we push forward, the innovative, open spirit that fuels our 140-year-old start-up culture and rapid growth also drives our personal growth. So, as we shape a more resourceful, less wasteful world, we build our careers too.  About the job As s Customer Quality Specialist you will own and drive the end-to-end customer claims process across our business unit. This means ensuring timely resolution of customer quality issues, reduction of claim costs, prevention of recurrence, and continuous improvement of customer satisfaction. You will lead the end-to-end customer claims process and work cross-functionally to improve customer experience, strengthen quality performance, and drive sustainable business improvements.  The role has cross-functional exposure and you will work closely with Operations, Product & Portfolio Management, R&D / Engineering, Supply Chain, Sales, Service, and Quality.  Key responsibilities:     Ownership of the end-to-end customer claims process towards full portfolio.     Standardize claim management practices across the BU.     Strengthen cross-functional accountability for corrective actions.     Increase customer confidence through proactive claim and escalation management     Follow up on claims and quality situations by making statistics, analysis and creating claims and quality reports.     Drive and manage quality improvement projects/activities.  Long term goals will be:     Reduce customer claim costs and quality-related business risks and enable leadership to focus on strategic priorities rather than operational intervention.     Drive systemic quality improvements through trend analysis and prevention.     Establish a scalable and sustainable claims management framework.  Networking and stakeholder engagement are important aspects of this role, which includes occasional domestic and international travel. You will be part of a team of three and report to Kubra Kucuk, who leads with trust, welcome creativity and are open to ideas to continuously develop our ways of working.  Who are you We are looking for you with a commercial mindset who is proactive, structured and have a curious mind to constantly find ways forward, driving for solutions and gaining results. This is not only an administrative role - but you will also have a big impact on business and customer satisfaction. The scope of this role is broad and diverse, requiring the ability to effectively prioritize competing demands while remaining resilient in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. If you enjoy engaging with people, building strong stakeholder relationships, and working in a global environment, you will thrive in this role. title: We need 2 rescue zookeeper in rescue zoo
description:
Are You Our Next Rescue Zookeeper at Odsherred Zoo Rescue?

We are looking for two qualified zookeepers with a passion for exotic animals and animal rescue!Fonden Odsherred Zoo Rescue is Denmark's first and only approved rescue centre for exotic animals in need. We provide a permanent home for animals that have experienced difficult circumstances and need specialised care.

We are currently looking for two dedicated, qualified zookeepers to join our team.

About the PositionsThe positions primarily involve caring for our larger animals and a variety of other species, including small wild cats, camels, meerkats, llamas, deer, birds and more.

Our rescue centre is home to approximately 600 animals, representing a wide range of exotic species.

You will work closely with our existing team of six zookeepers and a maintenance colleague. Teamwork is an essential part of our daily operations, and we expect everyone to contribute to a supportive and responsible working environment.

Both positions are full-time and include weekend duties approximately twice a month.

We are looking to fill:

  • One longer-term position, potentially permanent or lasting 1–2 years.

  • One shorter-term position, lasting approximately 6–12 months.

We would like the successful candidates to start as soon as possible.

What We Expect From You

We are looking for colleagues who are genuinely passionate about animal welfare and understand the responsibility that comes with working at a rescue centre.

You should be:

  • A qualified zookeeper with experience or a strong interest in exotic animals.

  • Reliable, punctual, honest and hardworking.

  • Positive, adaptable and willing to take responsibility.

  • A team player who actively supports and communicates with colleagues.

  • Observant and attentive to the animals in your care, recognising changes in their health, behaviour and general well-being.

  • Willing to learn and adapt to the different challenges of working with rescued animals.

  • Comfortable with the practical and sometimes physically demanding nature of animal care.

Teamwork is particularly important to us. We have a working culture in which colleagues help one another complete the day's responsibilities. We expect everyone to contribute, communicate openly and take their responsibilities seriously.

Working at a rescue centre is more than a traditional zookeeping job. It requires dedication, flexibility and an understanding that the needs of rescued animals can be very different from those of animals in conventional zoological collections.

Visitor Presentations and Social Media For approximately half the year, our rescue centre is open to the public.

During this period, all zookeepers participate in educational presentations for visitors, introducing the animals they care for and explaining their stories, behaviour and needs.

Public speaking is a mandatory part of the position, but previous presentation experience is not required as long as you are willing to learn.

We also regularly produce content for our social media platforms to raise awareness of our rescue work and the animals in our care.

This includes livestreams, photographs and recorded videos. Our zookeepers participate in this work by helping communicate the stories of the animals and the daily life of our rescue centre.

Understanding Our Mission, Odsherred Zoo Rescue is built around three main areas of work:

1. Rescue and Rehabilitation — Our Primary Mission

First and foremost, we are a rescue centre for exotic animals in need.

Our animals come from a variety of backgrounds, including the pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries, confiscations, former private ownership and other zoological institutions across Denmark and Europe.

Many of these animals have experienced difficult circumstances and require specialised care, patience and understanding.

Providing them with a safe and permanent home is our highest priority.

2. Conservation and Breeding Programmes

When resources and funding allow, we participate in conservation breeding programmes for rare and endangered species, including tamarins from South America.

Although this is an important part of our work, it remains secondary to our primary rescue mission.

3. Providing Homes for Surplus Zoo Animals

When we have the necessary space and resources, we also welcome surplus animals from other zoological institutions, providing them with a home when they might otherwise face euthanasia.

A Different Approach to Zookeeping, We want to emphasise that working at Odsherred Zoo Rescue is not the same as working at a traditional zoo.

We welcome applicants with experience from conventional zoological institutions, but it is essential that you are open-minded and willing to understand the different principles and challenges involved in operating a rescue centre.

Our focus is not simply on maintaining a zoological collection. It is on providing individual animals with the care, security and permanent home they deserve.

We are looking for colleagues who genuinely share these values and are willing to learn, adapt and contribute to our mission.

How to Apply, If you are passionate about exotic animals, dedicated to animal welfare and would like to become part of our rescue team, we would love to hear from you.

Please send your written application and CV to: post@odsherreds-zoo.dk only written inquiries.

Yours sincerely

Joan Thygesen

Director and founder of

Found Odsherred Zoo Rescue

title: Assistant Professors in Electronic Systems (with the possibility of tenure-track)
description:
At the Technical Faculty of IT and Design, Department of Electronic Systems, one or more positions as Assistant Professor in Electronic Systems are open for appointments from June 1, 2027, or soon after. The positions are available for a period of 4 years (with the possibility of tenure-track). The positions are with the department's research groups located at the university campus in Copenhagen.

Your profile and work tasksWe seek to appoint one or more Assistant Professors (with the possibility of Tenure-Track) to conduct research, teaching, and knowledge exchange, and to grow and develop the department's research activities within our subject fields.

The positions require internationally recognized research experience within one or more of the following areas:

  • Cyber security
  • Privacy engineering
  • Computer Systems
  • Edge/cloud computing
  • High-Performance Computing (HPC)
  • Data Engineering
  • Big Data Infrastructure
  • Machine Learning Systems

The main tasks and responsibilities include:

  • developing a research profile and providing valuable contributions to science.
  • providing research-based teaching and supervision within at least one subject area.
  • participating in grant application activities
  • coordinating own projects and contributing to an active academic environment

Your competenciesYou have an interest in collaborating with external partners and experience from participating in grant applications. You have also contributed to workplace well-being, collaboration, equal treatment, diversity, and a good working environment.

Selected candidates should demonstrate development potential in science and have peer-reviewed publications in recognized journals and books or anthologies. Under the leadership of others, you can plan and carry out individual teaching and supervision activities with a focus on the students' learning.

Who we areIn electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 700 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. 

The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. 

The department places significant emphasis on supporting early career researchers and provides comprehensive career and personal development programmes, specifically designed to assist individual academics in achieving their professional objectives.

You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

Qualification requirementsAppointment as Assistant Professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

Tenure-trackWhen appointing tenure track assistant professors, Aalborg University also place particular emphasis on:

  • The candidate can demonstrate a high degree of autonomy in their previous education and employment path
  • The candidate shows considerable potential and is among the best in their field
  • The candidate has academic experience from several universities and/or research institutions and preferably international experience
  • The candidate is a skilled communicator
  • The candidate writes and speaks English at the academic level
  • The candidate is expected to meet the criteria for permanent employment as an associate professor at Aalborg University at the end of the tenure track process

Evaluation and promotion proces:

  • Annual internal follow-ups to review progress on the promotion plan and ensure the assistant professor remains on track.
  • A mid-term evaluation, based on external review, conducted by an internal assessment committee after three years.
  • A final review by an external committee after 5.5 years. A positive outcome leads to a tenured appointment as Associate Professor.
  • Assessment in connection with transfer to associate professorship

Assessment in connection with transfer to associate professorshipThe assessment in connection with transition to tenure as an associate professor normally takes place in the final six months of the tenure track assistant professors’ employment. However, the employee may request that an assessment take place at an earlier time in the first four years. If this assessment finds that the employee is not academically qualified, they may request another assessment within the final six months of their period of employment. A maximum of two assessments may take place. 

The assessment, on transition to the associate professorship, will as a minimum, emphasize the following qualifications in relation to the scientific subject area of the tenure track assistant professorship: 

  • Research qualifications equivalent to the level that can be achieved on the basis of satisfactorily completed employment as tenure track assistant professor.
  • Documented scientific production at international level. Assessment will be based on up to ten selected publications selected by the employee.
  • Documentation of pedagogical supervision and upgrading of qualifications, including a positive written assessment of teaching qualifications. The assessment will also be based on the employee's teaching portfolio.
  • The level of contribution to an active academic environment as well as the ability to collaborate and build relationships.
  • The level of experience with grant proposals and experience of communicating research to relevant stakeholders. 

If the tenure track assistant professor fails to request that their qualifications be assessed in the last year of their period of employment or if they are assessed as not academically qualified, the university must immediately initiate dismissal proceedings in accordance with the collective agreement rules. 

How to apply  Your application must include the following: 

  • Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position 
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
  • Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma) 
  • List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications. 
  • Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this .
  • Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc. 
  • Additional qualifications in relation to the position 
  • References/recommendations 

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.    

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.  

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. The successful applicant is expected, with support from the university, to acquire Danish language skills over time and to be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 2–5 years of employment, including grading and supervising students, at a level corresponding to the teaching undertaken.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.      Further information Read more about our recruitment process here   

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.  

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. 

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Tenure track assistant professor/Tenure track researcher”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the worldAalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
